children: Federal Reserve Vice Chair of Supervision Michele Bowman on Tuesday said she expects inflation to cool next year as long as price pressures from the AI buildout and from the Middle East conflict recede.

"I think first we would have to see those risks being abated before I would be confident in my expectations for next year," Bowman said at the Council on Foreign Relations. "With the status of the labor market the way that it is and conditions as they have stabilized since last fall, I think we should be shifting our focus, or I certainly am shifting my focus, to inflation."
